source.title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions

accepted.question_text: For a fixed positive integer m, let F_m be the set of all nonzero even integers j with |j| <= m. A walk x from -n to n is a finite sequence of nonzero even steps x(t) whose total sum is 2n; writing the intermediate vertices as j(0) = -n and j(t) = -n + sum_{i=1}^t x(i), the walk is admissible when j(t) is never equal to ±n for 1 <= t <= ν, where ν + 1 is the number of steps. Let X_n^+(F_m) be the set of admissible walks from -n to n that use only positive steps from F_m, and for each such walk define h(x) = (∏_{t=1}^ν [n^2 - j(t)^2]^{-1})(∏_{t=1}^{ν+1} V(x(t))). For z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) ∈ C^m, define P_{m,n}(z) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x). Determine these polynomials P_{m,n}(z), and/or determine their asymptotic behavior for fixed m as n → ∞.
accepted.context_brief: Admissible walks with bounded even step sizes

accepted.question_text: Using the same family of admissible positive-step walks X_n^+(F_m) and the same weights h(x), decide whether for almost every parameter vector z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) ∈ C^m there exists a constant C(z) such that, for the relevant values of n, the inequality ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| <= C(z) * |∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)| holds. In other words, is the comparison condition appearing in Proposition 4 valid for almost all z in C^m?
accepted.context_brief: Almost-everywhere validity of the comparison bound

accepted.question_text: Take F = {-2, +4}, so R = 1 and S = 2, and let n = 2m + 1. For admissible walks from -n to n, let X_n(3) be the set of walks having exactly three negative steps equal to -2 and all remaining steps equal to +4. If h_1(x) = ∏_{t=1}^ν [n^2 - j(t)^2]^{-1}, define B_3(2m + 1) by B_3(2m + 1) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n(3)} h_1(x). Find an asymptotic formula for the sequence B_3(2m + 1), or at least prove that there exists an absolute constant C for which |B_3(2m + 1)| >= C^m / m!.
accepted.context_brief: Three negative steps in the {-2,+4} model

evidence.quote: Suppose F has just two elements, say F = {−2R, +2S} and V (−2R) = a, V (2S) = b. We are concerned on the polynomials (21) P_κ(a, b) = ∑_{x∈X_n(κ)} h(x), where X_n(κ) is the set of all admissible walks from −n to n with κ negative steps, i.e., x ∈ X_n(κ) if and only if (22) #{t : x(t) = −2R} = κ.
Otherwise, P_κ(a, b) = a^κ b^q B_κ(n), B_κ(n) = ∑_{x∈X_n(κ)} h_1(x).
Let F = {−2, +4}, i.e., R = 1, S = 2, and let n = 2m + 1.
Question 6. Find an asymptotic formula for the sequence B_3(2m+1), or at least explain that for some absolute constant |B_3(2m + 1)| ≥ C^m/m!.
